title: Combat Search and Rescue - Package
description: Package about the training that Combat Search and Rescue Airmen receive to prepare for their mission. Also see "Combat Search and Rescue, Parts 1 & 2" iin the b-roll section. Produced by Senior Airman David Zheng.
keywords: Combat Search and Rescue Airmen, Borger, Eric Schneck, Salvatore Sferrazza, training

transcript.text: Airmen, from the 64th Expeditionary Rescue Squadron, provide combat search and rescue
or CSAR support for forces serving in Operation Iraqi Freedom.
The pair of rescuement or PJs and helicopter crews train multiple times every week so they're
ready for any situation.
Well, we're here for a long period of time.
And if we're not staying current on our skills, kind of get dull.
So it's not just working to do it so you know how to go through it.
And so there's muscle memory.
So when you go out and launch on a real-world mission, you're ready to go.
There's no doubt in your mind.
Pinking through the steps is just happening automatically.
During training, CSAR Airmen practice alternate insertion and extraction methods.
The PJs fast-rope and repel out of the helicopter to recover the patient on the ground.
The training is designed to keep the team proficient at executing all their tasks.
Our mission is to ensure that our fellow Airmen have somebody there to pick them up when
they experience the worst day of their life.
You know, we're always making sure that we're 100% ready for the absolute worst-case
scenario.
The PJs spend their entire career getting ready for that event that is someone else's
bad day.
They exercise scenarios where they have to defeat a threat and train as realistically
as possible to live up to their motto that others may live.
Senior Airmen David Jung, Joint Base Belaud, Iraq.
